ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, LMNP is a rectangle, P is at the upper left, L is at the upper right, M is at the lower right, and N is at the lower left. Two diagonals PM and NL are drawn inside the rectangle, and they intersect at point J. The problem asks for ∠MPN, that is, the angle formed by PM and PN at point P. Reasoning: Let the rectangle coordinates be P=(0,h), N=(0,0), M=(w,0), L=(w,h). The intersection point J of the rectangle diagonals is (w/2,h/2). The vector from J pointing to M is (w/2,-h/2), and the vector from J pointing to N is (-w/2,-h/2); these two rays are symmetric about the vertically downward direction through J. Let θ=m∠MPN. Since ∠MPN is the angle between diagonal PM and vertical side PN, rays JM and JN each make an angle θ with the vertically downward direction, so m∠MJN=2θ. Given m∠MJN=35°, therefore 2θ=35°, θ=17.5°. So m∠MPN=17.5.

raw_record.question_text:
Use rectangle LMNP, parallelogram LKMJ to solve the problem.
If $m \angle MJN = 35,$ find $m \angle MPN$

method.method_draft: First read the image: LMNP is the rectangle with P upper left, L upper right, M lower right, N lower left, and the diagonals PM and NL meet at J. The asked angle MPN is the angle between diagonal PM and vertical side PN. From the text, use m∠MJN = 35. Assign coordinates P=(0,h), N=(0,0), M=(w,0), L=(w,h), so J, the intersection of the rectangle diagonals, is (w/2,h/2). Let θ = m∠MPN. The ray JM has direction (w/2,-h/2) and the ray JN has direction (-w/2,-h/2); these two rays are symmetric about the downward vertical through J. Each makes angle θ with that vertical, so m∠MJN = 2θ. Therefore θ = 35/2 = 17.5.

method.method_draft: First read the image: J lies at the intersection of diagonals PM and NL of rectangle LMNP, so P,J,M are collinear and N,J,L are collinear. From the text, m∠MJN = 35. Since JP and JM are opposite rays on the same diagonal, ∠PJN is supplementary to ∠MJN, so m∠PJN = 180 - 35 = 145. In rectangle LMNP, the diagonals PM and NL are equal and bisect each other, so their half-segments PJ and JN are equal. Thus triangle PJN is isosceles with vertex angle 145 at J. Its two base angles are equal, so m∠JPN = (180 - 145)/2 = 17.5. Because J lies on PM, ∠JPN is the same as ∠MPN, giving 17.5.
